{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#rem-design-matrix-products}
#### Products with the design matrix

The product $\mX\vb$ collects all the linear predictors
$\tp{\vx_i}\vb$ into a single $n \times 1$ vector:

$$
\mX\vb =
\begin{bmatrix}
\tp{\vx_1}\vb \\
\vdots \\
\tp{\vx_n}\vb
\end{bmatrix}
$$

The matrix $\tp{\mX}\mX$ is $p \times p$ and symmetric,
since $\tp{(\tp{\mX}\mX)} = \tp{\mX}\,\tp{(\tp{\mX})} = \tp{\mX}\mX$
(@thm-transpose-product).
It appears in the OLS estimator $\hat{\vb} = (\tp{\mX}\mX)^{-1}\tp{\mX}\vy$.

For example, with $n = 3$ observations, an intercept, and one predictor,

$$
\mX = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 \end{bmatrix},
\quad
\vb = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}:
\qquad
\mX\vb = \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 5 \\ 7 \end{bmatrix},
\qquad
\tp{\mX}\mX = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 6 \\ 6 & 14 \end{bmatrix}.
$$

:::
